reviews.title: Used to be the Best
reviews.text:
This was the greatest marine tracking app…but then with the updates over the past year, it’s been destroyed. Sure, the functionality may still be there but they’ve changed the map base layer options to ones that are utterly unreadable. 

It’s extremely difficult to differentiate between vessel types on the white water or the black water in dark mode. It’s also hard to distinguish between bland grey land and water - it plays tricks on the eyes. Water is blue on most maps and was on the previous map here. 

Now there are zero land details where before they actually had better land details than most land map apps - and I used it a lot for that purpose. I realize that’s not the focus of this app, but why get rid of something that can draw and retain users?

The vessel symbols have gotten smaller and the color difference between a tug boat and a cargo ship has become indistinguishable for two completely different kinds of vessels. 

Feature after feature is going behind paywalls. A paid premium membership isn’t even enough to get general information a non-industry person general interest information about the ship passing by the shore anymore. 

It’s so disappointing to see what once was a great app that could be enjoyed by shipspotters as well useful for professionals leave the shipspotters out in the cold. Though I can’t believe the design choices work for professionals either.

reviews.title: Old version more intuitive
reviews.text:
Hey there! I’ve had this app for nearly a decade when it was originally free and didn’t have a paywall and I did the update a couple months or so back. 

I want to like this new version, a lot. But man it’s been frustrating to have lost so much access that I previously had. 

When the update went through I was able to see all of the same things as before, including being able to track the vessel and its speed at a given time. Though I was given the whole, “thank you for being with us for so long, we appreciate it and you’ll still be able to use the app the same as before, nothing will change for you” this is false. I just started getting the paywall in the app and I’m a little miffed about it. The previous version allowed me to change the time depending on where I am and not just give UTC, this version does not. The previous version was snappy, if I clicked on something it immediately popped up, this version lags quite a bit. 

Overall, I’ve lost more from doing the switch than I’ve gained. Even if I were to pay for it now, the features on it that I DO have access to just seem……different, and not in a good way. reviews.title: World's # 1 to worlds worst in one update
reviews.text:
Used MarineTraffic for years and absolutely loved it, but the latest update has completely ruined the app.

The old layout was simple, clear and gave you all the information you needed at a glance. The new design is cluttered, harder to navigate and hides useful information behind multiple taps. The map is far less intuitive, vessel icons are harder to identify, and the overall user experience feels like a massive step backwards.

As someone who works at sea and relies on MarineTraffic regularly, the previous version was far superior. It feels like the redesign prioritised appearance over functionality.

Please listen to your long-term users and bring back the simplicity and usability that made MarineTraffic the best vessel tracking app available.

reviews.title: Avoid: Ruined since ownership change
reviews.text:
Step-change in both usability and features since update. This isn’t first major update comes since the acquisition of the app by parent company Kpler (2023). It seems that as in common with many such acquisitions an organisation buys a brand because it works well, is well liked and unique.  This is often due to a number of factors, including hubris, corporate vanity and lack
of management oversight; the brand is changed so it no longer fulfils the original criteria.  I’m not saying that this in-play here but it’s pretty common in every sector of business especially in the mobile IT world. Kpler; please look at what you bought and what you’ve done to it.  Even the recent 5-star reviews are critical.  Interesting that some of your responses to those are a bit odd.   Just saying.

reviews.title: Very Poor since reboot.
reviews.text:
I’ve used marine traffic as a support tool for work (marine pilotage scheduling and traffic logistics) for several years now and it’s been brilliant. However, since the update the tool has become virtually worthless. 

- The placing of certain tools (like a measuring/dividers feature) behind a much higher pay wall is a shame. 

- The overall look and interface of menus and vessels specifics now feels long winded and cluttered. 

- A distinct lack of filtering/personalisation on offer (e.g being able to set home location anywhere on the chart) meaning you have to ‘sift’ for information, generally slowing down the whole experience. 

I held onto the previous version for as long as possible as I’d been warned by colleagues of how poor the new version is and they were right. It’s gone from being a great quick reference guide we could use on a mobile devise to a clumsy, expensive mess.

reviews.title: Recent searches is unusable
reviews.text:
Since the rewrite, the Recent Searches feature has become significantly less useful.

First, none of the search history from the previous version appears to have been carried over, which meant losing a valuable record of frequently tracked vessels. More frustratingly, the new version seems to retain only around 14 recent searches, and even that list appears to refresh or overwrite entries unpredictably.

There is also no way to remove unwanted entries. If you search for a vessel, open it, and then realize it’s not the one you were looking for, it remains in your recent searches with no option to delete it. This quickly clutters the list and makes it harder to access vessels you actually want to track.

The previous implementation was far more useful for regular users. Please consider increasing the number of saved searches, making the history more persistent, and adding the ability to manually remove entries from the list.

I even signed up for the free trial to see if that was better, had the same zoom issues, plus the charts are so cluttered you really have to look to find vessels.  I clicked the remove ATONs to see if that cleaned it up, looked like nothing was removed at all. Marine Traffic development team, listen to your Mariners. reviews.title: Awful after recent update to 5.1.10
reviews.text: I work as a tugboat captain and have been using this app since I was in the maritime academy, over a decade ago. Since then I have loved it and it has been the go to tracking app. After automatically updating itself to the new version, I’m sad to say that it feels like a different app in all the worst ways. It can still show locations for ships using AIS, but not all will show up no matter if their AIS is working or not. Any ability to use vectors is now gone for basic or loyalty membership. With that in mind, most of the customization is also gone on the app. I used to be able to use the route tracking feature and had saved routes in there, but that has now been removed and put behind a paywall. The only thing that was “added” to my plan was weather tracking which I couldn’t care less about when compared to the many other features I had access to before. When trying to contact them to try and get some info on where to find some of the live data (vectors, angle indicators, etc.) that used to be there, their contact form said it couldn’t take an email address from aol, gmail, yahoo, or hotmail. It doesn’t say what, if any, email addresses would work so here I am leaving a poor review for a once great app. I can’t say I recommend this app to others, will be searching for a different one to use going forward, and hope everyone else does as well.

reviews.title: New Version is Aweful
reviews.text: Surprise surprise. I opened up MarineTraffic to locate a friend who is sailing in the Caribbean only to find that it’s been completely rewritten and nearly incomprehensible. The original version was clear and easy to use.  The new version is completely confusing. It’s hard to tell where water ends and land begins. And you can’t customize it, except for showing wind and waves.  Moreover, it has lost all of the saved vessels and ports that were in the original version. What were they thinking? It’s all very disappointing.

reviews.title: A Polished Downgrade Disguised as an Update
reviews.text:
This latest MarineTraffic update manages to achieve something impressive — it takes a previously clear and dependable reference tool and turns it into an unnecessarily frustrating experience.

The biggest issue appears when vessel names are enabled. AIS targets routinely disappear unless you zoom in excessively, making it impossible to maintain a useful overview of traffic. Instead of quickly understanding what’s happening in an area, you are forced into constant zooming just to confirm vessels are still there. This alone makes the app feel unreliable.

Vessel track viewing has also been severely degraded. What used to be an easy way to understand a vessel’s past speed and course is now vague and difficult to interpret. Information hasn’t been improved — it’s been obscured behind oversimplified visuals.

Equally frustrating is the decision to make all AIS targets the same size. Busy areas now appear as indistinguishable clusters of identical symbols, removing the visual hierarchy that previously allowed quick understanding of traffic density.

The new default map colours are another baffling decision. Sea and land are now so similar in tone that basic visual interpretation becomes harder than it should ever be. A marine reference app should prioritise clarity above all else, yet the default setup requires manual adjustment simply to reach the usability the previous version offered out of the box.

reviews.title: Backwards step
reviews.text:
I’m pretty sure I’ve not added a review prior to now, but I feel compelled to review this update.

I’ve got no idea whose feedback the developers listened to prior to releasing this, but I now find this Marine Traffic is horrible to use.  I don’t care about Fleets or whatever useless feature I’m supposed to be grateful for-I would just like maps that are as customisable as previous releases. The handful of options available now are a backwards step, and as far as I can see, are not even available if I pay to upgrade.

reviews.title: New update is rubbish
reviews.text:
Can no longer see the outline of the ships on the map. They just appear as a dot, so when they're docked I can't see which way they're facing. Also have to subscribe now to see the length of the ship. The new interface is over complicated and not as intuitive as is used to be. 
I use this app for work on docks, but won't be using anymore as it no longer does what I need. I've switched to vessel finder.

I'm not one to complain usually, but looking at the most recent reviews here and not one is positive. Not sure what you were thinking when you made a perfectly good app unusable for a lot of people.

reviews.title: Great App
reviews.text:
I used to use this app to track the progress of my partners boat when he had no mobile phone signal but annoyingly a couple of years ago that became a paid extra/subscription function.
Fast forward to today and I’ve deleted the app completely in favour of a competitor app which is free to use and actually works well!! Imagine that!! 
Marine traffic has gone too far with greed, useless updates and AI controlled responses to users questions/complaints….. their downfall is underway!

reviews.title: This app is now a POS
reviews.text:
I did not want to write a review, but it is impossible to reach the developer. I have used this app for several years and am currently a paid subscriber. Before this update, I could launch the app and be signed in seamlessly. I have yet to be able to login to the new app. I’m not going into all the issues I experienced, but I have tried all the usual ways to correct this type of problem. Nothing has worked. There isn’t even a screen where you can manually enter a password and email combination. No lost password link. Nothing helpful. Clicking on the “contact developer” link in the App Store takes you to the parent company’s website which contains no help links. Nada. 
This app isn’t worth downloading. Sorry.

reviews.title: Was fantastic, now… not so much.
reviews.text:
This used to be a fantastic app for vessel tracking. One where you could set up notifications for vessel movements/AIS changes easily as you set up vessels in “your fleet.” Now? It’s no where near as user friendly, to the point where I no longer have any idea where to go in the program to find those same notification settings. 

It’s also very glitchy in searches, where you no longer get a list of partial matches as you type in a vessel name (and often get “no results” when entering the full name of a vessel). Hopefully they revert back to the previous layout.

reviews.title: Horrible update.
reviews.text:
I’m a marine pilot and have been using this app daily on the job for years. Was an absolute critical and useful tool for safety of navigation. This update is probably the worst update to an app I’ve ever seen. Made the “Worlds #1 Ship Tracking App!” completely useless the “World’s Worst Ship Tracking App!”

Ships appear/disappear as you zoom so you can’t see concentrations of traffic; ships with time-late positions are no longer faded so ships may or may not be where you think they are; no longer do the tracks show relative size based on the size of the icon so a small 20’ vessel appears the same as a deep draft 1200’ ship; UI and menus are more cumbersome making it harder to find the information you need. 

I hope Marine Traffic managers are seeing the myriad of 1 star ratings and abysmal reviews since the update. They are rapidly losing customers that relied on this app for years - myself included. 

Simple fix - fire the programmers and go back to the previous version TODAY! Save your customer base before it’s too late and you lose them forever.

reviews.title: ZERO STARS would be more appropriate!
reviews.text: Latest update is very poor compared to the apps previous iterations. Not as many customisations available as previously and the information pages are poorly formatted, on both iPad and iPhone versions the vessel departure and eta times are obscured by further text on the page. This is extremely poor, why was the app not properly tested for functionality and usability prior to release?  Map scale has been removed from the map.  App now showing vessels underway in the middle of the desert.  Vessel positions no longer update/refresh automatically, refresh button on screen does not work. This so called UPDATE is appallingly poor.

reviews.title: Worst “Upgrade” of an app I’ve experienced
reviews.text: I don’t know what KPLER was thinking when they did this massive “upgrade” to the MarineTraffic app.  The user interface, as well as many of the features, have gone down the toilet. So disappointed. It was really a great app before. Went to the KPLER website and learned that it had acquired MarrineTraffic in 2023.  I know we have all seen this many times. Individual or small group develops a great app, keeps improving it. And then ultimately sells to a big company. I have no issue with people doing this, as they should be rewarded for their awesome product. It’s such a shame when the new company just destroys it.

reviews.title: ABANDON SHIP!! 🚢
reviews.text:
I don’t leave reviews very often, but I feel compelled to share my disappointment with the latest release of this app. Bring back the old version! After being a paid subscriber for several years, this “update” is a monumental failure and utterly disappointing. Clumsy interface….horrible map colour schemes…Whoever designed and approved this app wants sacking. This app used to be the “FlightRadar24” for the seas. Not any more. ☹️Subscription cancelled. ⛔️You have lost another loyal customer in the name of progress, and looking at the latest feedback it doesn’t look like I’m the only one. ABANDON SHIP! 👋
I’ve moved to VesselFinder Lite and am loving it. It does what I need.

reviews.title: What the heck did they do?
reviews.text: I’ve been using this app on my iPad for the past year.  I live near the sea and was always wondering about the many ships and boats I see.  I loved this app but after this past update?  I hate it!  It’s like being on an ancient desktop computer back in the 90s.  The graphics are awful.  It’s not finding ships that are sitting right in front of me.  Or telling me outright that they don’t exist.  The maps are useless.  Fortunately, it’s still working properly on my iPhone and I will be sure to not allow any updates on it!  Put it back the way it was!  I was planning on upgrading my account to have a paid one.  Not any more!

reviews.title: Disastrous update
reviews.text: The latest update has really spoiled what for years I have found a really good app. The visual display is dreadful and it is really challenging to quickly find the basic information about ships.  I have run the app successfully and smoothly on my iphone and ipad for almost 10 years but now whilst I’m able to log in on my iphone, it won’t even load on my ipad and give me the log in page.  I too am looking for an alternative as I’m sick of trying with this one. (It was even challenging writing this review as the system kept rejecting all the nicknames I came up with).

reviews.title: Don’t update or download the new version
reviews.text: I’ve used this app for several years now and was a fan. The update has ruined a very useful application and removed many of the useful features. The map colours make it difficult to differentiate between land and sea. The ship sizes don’t indicate the actual size of the vessel. The ship positions are inaccurate. Features like vessels near me are missing and looking for vessels near one you are looking at return vessels 10’s of miles away. I’m looking for another app.
